events.description: Completion of the asphalt/concrete production plant and road machinery delivery in Kabul under Soviet assistance.
Completion of the combined grain/bread factory in Kabul and the grain elevator in Puli-Khumri.
Completion of the river port at Shirkhan, expanded in 1961.
Completion of the Bagram airdrome with a 3,000 m landing strip.
Completion of the Kabul international airdrome and the Puli-Khumri power station.
Completion of the Salang highway and tunnel across the Hindu Kush, and three Kunar bridges in Nangarhar.
Completion of the Kushka-Herat-Kandahar highway, the Kabul-Jabl-us-Seradzh highway, and the Jalalabad irrigation channel and power station.
Completion of the Naghlu Dam and Power Station and the Doshi-Shir Khan highway.
Completion of the gas transmission line from the gas deposit to the USSR border (98 km).
Establishment of the Shibergan gas production facility and geological surveying in northern Afghanistan.
Completion of the Puli-Khumri–Mazar-e-Sharif–Shibergan highway and the Khairaton branch road.
Completion of the Mazar-e-Sharif nitrogen fertilizers plant and the Amu-Darya gas line extension.
Completion of the Shindad airdrome with a 2,800 m strip.
Completion of the Amu-Darya auto and railway bridge and installation of the Intersputnik Lotus satellite unit.
Oil production in Logar and eight technical vocational schools completed.
Completion of the Kamaz truck service station in Khairaton and other facilities.
Completion of the Institute for Social Sciences under the PDPA Central Committee.
Reconstruction of the Salang tunnel's technical systems and 220 KW lines from the Soviet border to Kunduz and Mazar-e-Sharif.
Completion of the Ministry of Interior base in Khairaton for loading and storage of special freights.
Agreement on technical aid (state credit) covering the Sangilyan barium lode and Dzharkuduk oil lode drilling.
Agreement (state credit) covering Kabul-Khairaton road restoration and geological surveys.
Agreement (state credit) for a blood transfusion station, first phase operational 21 April 1987.
Agreement covering Kabul Airport reconstruction, Shirkhan-Kunduz power line, and Ainak plant design work.
Correspondence between the sides (state credit) on reconstruction of the Turgundi railway station.
Agreement (state credit) covering Kabul telephone/telegraph stations, Shibergan housing, Dzhangalak auto repair plant, northern oil drilling, Mazar-Kabul power line.
Agreement (state credit) on seed production labs, Jalalabad agricultural technical school and veterinary services.
Correspondence between Soviet and Afghan sides on Ainak copper enrichment plant design and survey.
Agreement on Turgundi railway station reconstruction (state credit).
Agreement on seed production, agricultural school, veterinary services, and related projects (state credit).
Agreement on drilling 45 artesian wells and erecting 115 wells (state credit).
Agreement on power station feasibility study, textile plant restoration, Kokcha cotton plantation (state credit).
Agreement on three TV stations in Kabul (state credit).
Agreement on ten technical schools and one industrial teaching school for 4000 students.
Agreement on beginning operation of 20 Moskva-type TV stations (state credit).
Trade and Pay Agreement regulating Soviet-Afghan trade, with payments in US dollars via clearing.
Soviet-Afghan agreement covering many projects (dams, cotton plants, factories) later halted.
Agreement covering six northeastern airdromes, Ainak mining enterprise, oil wells and refinery, later halted.
Soviet-Afghan goods turnover totalled 1,124 million rubles.

key_claims: Soviet technical assistance built much of Afghanistan's infrastructure from the 1950s: roads, airfields, the Salang tunnel, gas fields and power stations.
Afghanistan's imports were practically completely satisfied by Soviet supplies, and the USSR's share of Afghan foreign trade reached about 60% by 1987, up from 28% in 1977.
Natural gas, carbide and canned olives from joint sites were exported exclusively to the USSR.
Several projects were halted by the mid-1980s, some with reduced scope, and some were left as survey work only.
Soviet-Afghan trade is described as stabilizing the Afghan situation and supporting the PDPA's policy of 'national appeasement'.
Soviet exports to Afghanistan far exceeded Afghan exports, producing a persistent Afghan trade debt.
Natural gas made up 57% of Afghan exports to the USSR in 1987 but declined due to well depletion.
Afghan private merchants shifted toward third countries for convertible currency, supplying the USSR reluctantly.
The USSR provided free aid, subsidies and credit extensions, and reduced Afghan debt to 103 million rubles by January 1988.
Soviet credits were redirected away from projects lacking security, such as the Salang bypass and northern irrigation sites.
